summary.text: An 83-year-old man was referred with suspected serous retinal detachment of the left eye. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in the right eye and 20/17 in the left, intraocular pressure was normal, and the anterior segments and fellow eye showed no findings. Fundus photography showed an elevated choroidal mass with posterior vitreous detachment; angiography, MRI (tumor 5.9×5.7 mm base, 4.1 mm thick) and SPECT characterized it, and PET/CT showed no distant metastases.

Choroidal melanoma was diagnosed clinically and treated with stereotactic hypofractionated radiotherapy, 60 Gy in 5 fractions, in January 2021. Five months later he developed visual deterioration and distortion with BCVA 20/50, and OCT showed a full-thickness stage 4 macular hole with cystic cavities; about 2 weeks later an acute massive vitreous hemorrhage lowered BCVA to 20/2000.

Repeat PET/CT showed no significant abnormalities or metastases, so a vitrectomy with inverted ILM peeling and gas-fluid exchange with 20% sulfur hexafluoride was performed, closing the macular hole. The vitreous hemorrhage reappeared 2 weeks later and a second vitrectomy followed after 4 months of observation.

The macular hole remained closed after both procedures, the retina stayed attached, the tumor showed marked regression and BCVA improved to 20/125. No intraocular tumor dissemination or distant metastases were found during follow-up.
